thread:
Maria Nguyen: Quick FYI — customers are seeing odd quota/route behavior after upgrading to ts-sdk@3.0. They set `routingPolicy: 'latency'` but requests are landing on fallback models and console shows 'unknown route' telemetry. Anyone else? :thinking:

Kevin Patel: I saw one report from ACME earlier. Looks like the exported type name changed in the SDK, we accidentally renamed the enum value to `latency_prefer` in the build step. The runtime still expects `latency`.

Zara Lee: Oof. Did we publish without a deprecation warning?

Kevin Patel: Yep — the change slipped past the compatibility tests because TS types compiled differently and our runtime does a string compare. No runtime validation on the SDK side.

James O'Connor: Can you paste the minimal repro? I want to see how the console telemetry surfaces this — whether it's flagged as a client error or a routing mismatch.

Maria Nguyen: Repro:
```ts
// old (works)
client.generate({
  model: 'redwood-llama-7b',
  routingPolicy: 'latency',
  input: 'Summarize my README'
})

// after upgrade (breaks)
client.generate({
  model: 'redwood-llama-7b',
  routingPolicy: 'latency_prefer', // new enum value in ts-sdk@3.0
  input: 'Summarize my README'
})
```

Olivia Chen: From the infra side the router returns a 200 but marks the request as "routed_to_fallback" when it sees unknown policy. Console telemetry shows fallback counts but the SDK didn't warn, so app owners think it's a quota/regression.

Kevin Patel: Short-term fix: push 3.0.1 that restores the old literal and emits a console.warn when an unknown policy is supplied. Long-term: we should accept aliases server-side and return a clear 4xx with reason so telemetry can show "client misconfiguration" instead of silent fallback.

Zara Lee: Agree. Also let's add an SDK migration guide in the release notes and a small check in our release pipeline that runs a smoke test against the routing enum values.

James O'Connor: I'll file an incident-esque release note and ping support docs. Action items: Kevin — patch the SDK + warn, Olivia — add server aliasing + clearer reason codes, Maria/Zara — docs + release note. ETA?

Kevin Patel: I can do the SDK patch today and cut 3.0.1.

Olivia Chen: I'll add an alias map and a distinct metric tag `client_error=invalid_routing_policy` so we can slice it in dashboards.

Maria Nguyen: Perfect. Zara can you draft the short "how to migrate" snippet for the Console changelog? Something like: 'If you upgraded to ts-sdk@3.0 and see unfamiliar fallbacks, change `routingPolicy: "latency_prefer"` back to `"latency"` or upgrade to 3.0.1.'

Zara Lee: Yep — will have a PR up in ~90m.

deploy-bot: deploy triggered: ts-sdk v3.0.1 (patch) — build queued. :rocket:

James O'Connor: Thanks team. Once Olivia has the metric we can create an alert on a spike of `client_error=invalid_routing_policy` and surface it in the Console rollout UI as a migration blocker.

Maria Nguyen: Adding that to the rollout checklist. Appreciate the quick turnaround :thumbsup:

Kevin Patel: Also adding a unit test to prevent future renames from sneaking into the published package (assert the compiled JS contains the literal values).
